description: FS-GG typed coordination engine — the schedulability model behind `fsgg-coord` as one total function over a board-state snapshot, plus the typed IO layer that drives it. It IS the coordination tool (ADR-0034/ADR-0040): the `fsgg-coord` shim resolves and execs it; there is no bash left to shadow.
releaseNotes:
0.15.0 — MINOR on the 0.x line, which is also the 0.x BREAKING signal.

TEN engine commits since 0.14.0, and ONE OF THEM MOVES THE WIRE SURFACE
(src/FS.GG.Coord.Core/Protocol.fs). That file is the source the exit-code tables in every worker-facing
skill are GENERATED from, so between .github#1680 landing and this release the org's own documents
described a verb contract no published engine implemented. This release is what makes them true again.

THE REASON TO TAKE THIS RELEASE: every worker vendors `scripts/fsgg-coord`, which resolves and execs
this package. A receiver on 0.14.0 runs a collision gate that answers DISJOINT over live locks, a
`landable` that burns 600 seconds waiting on already-merged work, and an `add` that files rows no
scheduler can see.

BREAKING — THE WIRE SURFACE. `landable` answers a PR THAT IS NOT OPEN with exit 10 (.github#1680).
GitHub reports mergeable as null on a merged PR, which the four-row match read as "still computing" and
returned as `pending` / exit 7 — the ONE code the contract defines as worth retrying, for the most
terminal state there is. So the waiting form spent its entire 600s budget (30 tries x 20s) on a settled
fact, every time, and the caller that meets this most is the RECOVERY path, which re-gates a PR whose
worker died between merge and stamp.

  $ fsgg-coord-engine landable 1675 --wait
      0.14.0:  pending   rc=7    after 600s
      0.15.0:  merged    rc=10   after 0.69s

Exit 10 prints one of two words on stdout and they call for OPPOSITE acts. `merged` means the work
LANDED: do not merge it again, go STAMP it. `closed` means nothing landed: do NOT stamp it done. It is
deliberately not 3 (red/conflicted), because folding a success into the stop code would tell that
successor to give up rather than to finish.

WHO THIS BREAKS: any caller that switched exhaustively over `landable`'s previous five codes, or that
treated "not 0 and not 7" as a failure. Exit 10 on `merged` is a SUCCESS. An unmet `--sha` on the merged
arm is now reported with its own sentences rather than dropped.

BREAKING — THE #353 COLLISION GATE REFUSES WHERE IT USED TO PERMIT. Three fixes, one surface:
`widen`, `set-paths` and `overlap --active`.

  * .github#1740 — the scan was served from the 90-second scheduling cache, and a `Status` write can sit
    QUEUED on an exhausted budget, so the freshest possible board still showed the pre-claim column.
  * .github#1779 — the candidate set is no longer derived from the board at all. `claim` exits GREEN with
    that column unwritten in FOUR ways and the cache/queue fixes could reach only two. The scan now keys
    on the LOCK: `Reads.openIssues` lists open issues with their bodies in one paginated call, token
    conflicts are computed on those free bodies, and a marker is read only for a row that actually
    collides. Measured either side of one `overlap --active` on the live board: 24/27/31 GraphQL points
    and the wrong answer, to 0/0/0 points and the right one.
  * .github#1792 — `Scan.snapshot` asked `reserver` (a lapsed lease still reserves) while the collision
    gate asked `winner` (it does not), so "is this file reserved?" had two answers depending on which
    verb asked. The gate asks a reservation question and now calls the reservation function.

  $ fsgg-coord-engine widen .github#123 --paths src/A.fs
      0.14.0:  DISJOINT   (over a live, uncolumned claim on src/A.fs)
      0.15.0:  OVERLAP

WHO THIS BREAKS: anything that read DISJOINT as licence to edit. There is no CAS on a file, so nothing
downstream ever re-decided that answer — which is why a wrong DISJOINT was final and this is the fix
worth taking the release for. Two workers really did edit one file this way on 2026-07-28.

BREAKING — READS FAIL CLOSED (.github#1794). `Reads.openIssues` DROPPED an element with no numeric
`number` silently, and read an absent or ill-typed `body` as an empty string — which parses as
"declares nothing" and collides with nothing. Both failed OPEN, into the gate above, where a wrong
DISJOINT is final. Now an unidentifiable element refuses the whole read quoting `element N of M`, and an
unreadable body is carried to the marker phase: no reserver means it is safely skipped, a reserver means
we may not answer DISJOINT over a live reservation, so it refuses and names the row and the holder.
`body: null` stays a real observed empty body. Calls that exited 0 over a partially unreadable board now
exit non-zero — that is the point of the change, not a regression.

BREAKING — `who` GAINS A FOURTH ROW STATE (.github#1668). `Reads.markers` classified every comment as
marker-or-nothing, so two failures to READ were indistinguishable from a successful observation of
ABSENCE, and `Ok []` on an In-progress row rendered as `UNCLAIMED` with the "someone is working outside
the protocol" accusation attached. That was printed 32 seconds before a `--force` deleted a live marker
on the same item. `who` now has `UNDETERMINED`, with a distinct `.state` word in `--json`, no
accusation, and an explicit instruction not to dispatch, `reap` or `adopt`. The incompleteness rides
EVERY row, not only markerless ones: a hidden marker with a lower id makes a `held` row name the wrong
holder. Consumers switching exhaustively over the state vocabulary meet a new value (residue: #1897).

BREAKING — `FSGG_CLAIM_LEASE_MIN` IS ACTUALLY READ (.github#1677). It was named across this repo as the
way to configure the claim lease and honoured by no line of code; `--lease` was the only control that
ever existed. Precedence is now `--lease` then `FSGG_CLAIM_LEASE_MIN` then 120. A malformed value is
REFUSED (exit 1, naming the variable and what was read), identically to `--lease abc` — deliberately,
because falling back to 120 on garbage would rebuild the exact unfalsifiability this fixes. Unset and
empty mean "not configured" and take the default.

WHO THIS BREAKS: anyone who exported the variable and got 120 anyway. They now get the lease they asked
for, which may not be the lease their scripts were tuned against.

BREAKING for board writers — `add` DEFAULTS `Status` TO `Backlog` (.github#1823). A row with no `Status`
is invisible to every scheduler. Fourteen were filed that way on 2026-07-28, in three batches, and every
one was found by accident. `Backlog` and not `Ready`: visible to triage, not startable without a
deliberate promotion. THE DEFAULT ONLY EVER FILLS AN EMPTY COLUMN — `add` is idempotent and re-run
routinely, so the already-on-board arm reads the column first and an unreadable column is left alone
rather than defaulted. `add` never becomes a refusal: an underivable identity degrades the column by
name instead of refusing the filing. Ships with the `STATUS-UNSET` chore, which reports rather than
prevents.

CHANGED DIAGNOSTICS — A SECONDARY RATE LIMIT IS TOLD FROM THE PRIMARY BUDGET (.github#1666). `EX_RATE`
halted a six-worker fan-out repeatedly while the primary REST budget read 62%, 87%, 88% free, and a
retry seconds later succeeded. Four diagnoses were filed on that reading; three were withdrawn by their
own authors. There was never an internal counter — `Budget.classify` reacts to a real 403, computed
which of five wordings matched, discarded that, and rendered ONE sentence for THREE mechanisms. A
secondary (abuse-detection) limit is triggered by burst CONCURRENCY, fires with the primary counter
untouched, and NEVER APPEARS IN /rate_limit; the reset was being read off the primary window, which is
why "resets in ~6m" preceded a retry that succeeded in seconds; and `Retry-After`, the only header that
describes a secondary limit, was read nowhere. `RateLimitResource` now carries the mechanism and the
bucket, `SecondaryLimit` gets no resetAt, and the remedy is stated correctly: reduce concurrency, do not
wait fleet-wide. An unclassifiable 403 fails closed. `budget` now says whose budget it reports and what
it omits. The same defect was found and fixed in three more sites (Board, Scan, Done), which classified
GraphQL error arrays with `isRateLimited` and advised "REST-only work may still run" into the detector
that had just fired.

ALSO: a comment-only correction in the `command-contract` emitter (.github#1654) — it argued against a
schema bump using an asymmetry .github#1574 had already removed. No behaviour moves.
